rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heavy fan-out prompts get body recovery callout
rules_evaluated.evidence: "**Long session, long read.** Claude reviews the whole scrollback in one shot. If the review stalls or runs past a couple of minutes, interrupt with `Esc`, narrow to the orient and introspect phases first, and say `continue`."
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: The compound-and-close-1 prompt is a heavy full-scrollback review (matches the rule's "read-everything-in-X / full-history audit" signal), and the callout above it names recovery for only one failure direction (stall/over-run -> interrupt/narrow/continue). It's missing the required premature-stop naming: a shallow single-pass review that Claude confidently declares complete, with the paste-ready nudge ("there's more here"/"tell me what you've found so far, then continue"). The maintainer's "retro confabulation" watch-for is adjacent but not the same failure (ungrounded name-dropping in the summary vs. an incomplete read declared done) and isn't student-visible anyway (it's inside the maintainer HTML comment).
